item.title: The keys to the Internet change on October 11. Are you ready? (9 minute read)
item.description: The DNS root is scheduled to switch to KSK-2024 on October 11, and DNSSEC-validating resolvers that lack the new trust anchor could fail to resolve otherwise healthy websites. RFC 8509 sentinel queries let operators check readiness, although an unsupported sentinel test produces an inconclusive result rather than proving the key is missing.

item.title: Kubelet watches inodes. Just not until it's an emergency (11 minute read)
item.description: Kubelet's background image garbage collection only monitors disk bytes, so workloads heavy on small files receive no early intervention before kubelet evicts pods. On one node, unpacked layers from a single-stage build containing the @mui/icons-material package consumed millions of inodes. A multi-stage Dockerfile can reduce the deployed image from more than 40,000 files to a few dozen. Adding a Prometheus alert for inode usage above 80% can catch the problem well before the 95% eviction threshold.

item.title: Beyond synthetic testing: Capturing and replaying real database workloads at Airbnb (10 minute read)
item.description: Airbnb captures production SQL traffic at ProxySQL and reconstructs transaction order and timing for controlled replay against test databases. The system supports capacity planning and upgrade comparisons, uncovering MySQL 8.0 performance regressions and queries whose results depended on unspecified row ordering.

item.title: What is Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST)? (9 minute read)
item.description: Interactive application security testing instruments running applications to find issues like SQL injection and XSS with fewer false positives. It suits QA and staging but needs runtime agents, adds overhead, and scales poorly across microservices, so mature programs pair it with SAST and SCA.

One benchmark scaled concurrent Python sessions from 80 to 240 by offloading dormant memory to disk.

item.title: Proactive Defense: Hardening Code Pipelines and CI/CD Infrastructure (15 minute read)
item.description: Ephemeral runners, short-lived OIDC credentials, immutable dependency references, and provenance verification limit opportunities for software supply-chain compromise. Isolating build caches by branch privilege, blocking untrusted pull requests from release secrets, and quarantining incoming dependencies help prevent malicious code from reaching trusted builds.

item.title: The Shift to cgroup v2 in Kubernetes: What You Need to Know (8 minute read)
item.description: Kubernetes v1.35 defaults to refusing kubelet startup on cgroup v1 nodes, making migration to cgroup v2 an operational upgrade concern. Teams should check kernel and runtime compatibility, align kubelet and runtime cgroup drivers, and update monitoring tools that read cgroup files directly.

item.title: How fast is Python 3.15? (10 minute read)
item.description: Informal CPU-bound benchmarks of Python 3.15.0rc3 show standard-interpreter performance largely unchanged from 3.14, while the experimental JIT runs roughly 20–28% faster than the standard 3.15 interpreter. Free-threaded builds deliver substantial gains in four-thread tests, but these results cover only Fibonacci and bubble-sort workloads rather than general application performance.

Additional gains came from pagination, concurrent rendering, request hedging, compact embeddings, and fixing service-mesh connection bottlenecks.

item.title: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports metadata pre-filtering for higher recall on filtered searches (5 minute read)
item.description: AWS has introduced metadata pre-filtering for Amazon S3 Vectors to improve recall on filtered queries. The feature evaluates metadata filters before running a similarity search and supports up to 100 filter constraints per query. On highly selective filters, pre-filtering returns up to five times more matching vectors than previous methods. It is available immediately at no additional cost and works on existing indexes without requiring data re-ingestion.

item.title: Cloudflare Containers, rebuilt to scale agent sandboxes (15 minute read)

The update introduces a new scheduling policy that starts containers six times faster, with median startup times falling from over four seconds to 648 milliseconds in independent benchmarks. A filesystem snapshots feature is also available in public beta to let workspaces save and restore their state.

item.title: Building a post-quantum certificate authority with Merkle Tree Certificates (10 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare is launching a certificate authority that will support Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs), targeting early 2027 for inclusion in Chrome's Quantum-resistant Root Store. The company will provide standard MTC issuance at no cost. MTCs batch certificates into an append-only Merkle tree to address the scaling issues of post-quantum cryptography, which can increase log storage requirements by 40 times. Cloudflare successfully tested the technology with Chrome, serving billions of MTCs and finding that median performance was 9% faster than classical signature chains.

item.title: We tested our own WAF with frontier AI models. Here's what we found (9 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare built a dynamic testing tool that uses large language models to iterate attack payloads against its Web Application Firewall. The system ran 1,107 attempts across six attack categories and recorded 49 findings that required human review. Cloudflare used these results to release new detections for SSRF attacks and improve an existing cloud metadata rule.

It renders video by seeking frames in headless Chrome to ensure the same input always produces the same output.

item.title: How Uber Protects Against Retry Storms (12 minute read)
item.description: Uber added error ownership to its shared service-mesh infrastructure, so upstream services can distinguish failures they caused from errors merely propagated from deeper dependencies. During a major outage, the mechanism prevented an estimated 9.5 million unnecessary retry requests and reduced the maximum retry-storm radius across user-facing APIs from as high as 25 hops to 3.

The platform also supports Kubernetes deployment, GPUs, and Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust SDKs.

item.title: Pageindex (GitHub Repo)

item.title: Can your Postgres survive a bad query? (16 minute read)
item.description: Postgres memory limits such as work_mem apply per execution node and per worker rather than per query, allowing seemingly ordinary queries to consume many times the configured amount of memory. Recursive queries can be even more dangerous because some executor hash tables cannot spill to disk, creating workloads that can exhaust memory despite conservative configuration.

Effective tools need deployment event awareness, behavior captured from real traffic rather than specs, automatic handling of non-deterministic fields, and cross-service diff visibility, with eBPF-based traffic capture cited as one approach.
